clean_repro.probe: Create collection, insert 10 entities, search, delete 5 entities, search again without explicit consistency level
clean_repro.observed: Search after delete returns all 10 entities (including deleted ones) when using default consistency level
clean_repro.evidence_cmd: python -c "from pymilvus import MilvusClient; client = MilvusClient(host='localhost', port='19530'); client.create_collection('test_default', dimension=4, metric_type='L2'); client.insert('test_default', [{'id': i, 'vector': [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]} for i in range(10)]); client.load_collection('test_default'); print(client.search('test_default', [[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]], 10, output_fields=['id'])); client.delete('test_default', 'id in [1,2,3,4,5]'); print(client.search('test_default', [[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]], 10, output_fields=['id']))"

verified_assumptions: Search before delete returns all 10 entities
Search after delete should only return 5 entities (0,6,7,8,9) but returns all 10

contract_refs: Consistency level should control timestamp synchronization between delete and search operations
Default collection consistency level is Bounded (value=2)
Source: internal/proxy/util.go line 1319-1329: parseGuaranteeTsFromConsistency function shows Bounded should subtract graceful time from timestamp

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: SearchRequest → useDefaultConsistency=true → parseGuaranteeTsFromConsistency(Bounded) → should subtract graceful time from timestamp to ensure delete visibility
source_grounding.note: Source code shows proper consistency handling logic exists for default consistency level, but REST v2 search appears to bypass this when useDefaultConsistency is true and no explicit consistency_level is provided in request

falsification.probe: Test with explicit consistency level setting vs. default
falsification.observed: When consistency_level='Strong' explicitly set in search request: returns 5 results (correct). When using default (no consistency_level specified): returns 10 results (incorrect - stale data). This proves the bug is in the default consistency path, not in the underlying search mechanism.

excluded: Environment issue - tested multiple times with same result
Request parameter error - delete succeeds with correct count
API semantics misunderstanding - explicit consistency_level works correctly

cognition_match.developer_quote: REST v2 and gRPC divergent validation: REST v2 accepting values the gRPC path rejects (maintainers treat cross-channel inconsistency as a defect and fix it)
cognition_match.note: This bug hits the 'REST v2 API' blindspot - inconsistent behavior between REST v2 and gRPC paths for consistency enforcement. Maintainer cognition explicitly identifies this as a defect pattern.

verdicts.rationale: CONFIRMED: Search operations using default collection consistency level (Bounded) fail to enforce timestamp synchronization after delete, returning stale deleted entities. Source code analysis shows proper logic exists (parseGuaranteeTsFromConsistency) but REST v2 path bypasses it when useDefaultConsistency=true. Falsification test proves explicit consistency_level='Strong' works correctly, isolating the bug to the default consistency enforcement path. This matches maintainer blindspot for 'REST v2 API data type serialization/validation issues' (blindspot_indicators).
